IBM WBI-FN MSIF: dumps occur when used with DB2 V10 - APAR PM39949 needed - United States

MSIF; DB2 FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 MSIF execution group dumps with "failed to allocate memory" when WBI-FN runs with DB2 V10. 

CONTENT
When running MSIF with DB2 V10, the MSIF execution group dumps after processing several transfers with abend indication "failed to allocate memory". 

DB2 identified the problem to be a memory leak in DB2 V10 ODBC. 

If you use the MSIF service, please make sure that a Fix for APAR PM39949 - currently available as ++APAR AM39949 - is installed with DB2 V. 10 

Please request the APAR fix via a PMR for DB2.

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The IBM MQ classes for Java have been updated such that the
   WebSphere MQ v7.0.4.4 File Transfer Edition embedded agent can
   successfully query the level of IBM MQ Java client code that is
   available in the IBM Integration Bus execution group environment
   in which it is running.
   
   A code change has also been made to the WebSphere MQ File
   Transfer Edition Embedded Agent such that, if the IBM MQ Java
   client code cannot be queried from the environment, the Embedded
   Agent can still start.  In this scenario, the WebSphere MQ File
   Transfer Edition Embedded Agent will report blank version
   information for the IBM MQ Java client.
   
   ---------------------------------------------------------------
   The fix is targeted for delivery in the following PTFs:
   
   Version    Maintenance Level
   v7.0       7.0.4.6
   v8.0       8.0.0.3

STEP 1: SELF-GUIDED TROUBLESHOOTING


There are 2 types of memory used by IBM Integration Bus, native heap memory and JVM heap memory. The process for resolving issues with growth of each of these types of memory is different and so the first step is to determine what type of memory is growing. 

To determine the amount of JVM heap used follow these steps: 
 * In IBM Integration Explorer right click on the problematic execution group and select Statistics -> Start Resource Statistics 
 * Right click the problematic execution group and select Statistics -> View Resource Statistics 
 * In the Resource Statistics Table View select "JVM" 
 * You may need to wait up to 20 seconds for the first Resource Statistics Publication to arrive 
 * The value under the column CommittedMemoryInMB shows the size of the JVM Heap

Start tracing of broker agent and execution groups 

1. Start Trace


mqsichangetrace <brokername> -t -b -l debug 
mqsichangetrace <brokername> -t -e <egroup> -l debug -r 

where <brokername> is the name of your broker while <egroup> is the name of your execution group


2. Deploy and monitor for errors.

3. Stop all tracing when deploy errors occur. 

mqsichangetrace <brokername> -t -b -l none
mqsichangetrace <brokername> -t -e <egroup> -l none


Format the traces using the commands below:

1. Retrieve the trace log for the specified component. 
mqsireadlog <brokername> -t -b agent -f -o agenttrc.xml

2. Retrieve and format the XML log 
mqsiformatlog -i agenttrc.xml -o agenttrc.txt

3. Retrieve the trace log for the specified component. 
mqsireadlog <brokername> -t -e <egroup> -f -o <egroup>.xml

4. Format the XML log file 
mqsiformatlog -i <egroup>.xml -o <egroup>.txt

5. After a PMR is open, submit the files agenttrc.txt and <egroup>.txt to IBM Support for problem determination.

4. 
 5. Traces If the problem occurs during a runtime test or with the Toolkit test facility, WMB execution group traces [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321] can be used to gain a better understanding of the problem.  * A user level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21663024#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed. It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
     * A service level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21663024#2] is intended to be provided to IBM Support to assist in the diagnosis of your issue.
    
    
 6. 
 7. For issues with high CPU:  * A report or screen capture showing usage.
     * Console dumps.
       Collect two console dumps (approximately two to three minutes apart) of the address space exhibiting the high CPU while the high CPU is occurring.
       See: Using the DUMP command on z/OS [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/an04350_.htm]
    
    
 8. 
 9. For issues with high memory usage:  * A report or screen capture showing usage.
     * SVC Dumps.
       Collect an SVC dump after EG has stabilized but still showing growth.
       See: Using the DUMP command on z/OS [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/an04350_.htm]
